newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau media get threats to stop reporting on triad.
newsitem.headline: Macau media get threats to stop reporting on triad.

text.p: Threatening, anonymous letters have sent a stern warning to journalists in crime-hit Macau -- stop reporting on the 14K "triad" gang and its leader.

Tiny Macau, a Portuguese-run territory of 455,000 people on China's southern coast, has been hit by a crime wave linked to a turf war between two main triad or criminal societies -- the 14K and Soi Fong -- that has left 15 people dead so far this year.

"Warning, from today it is not allowed to mention Wan Kwok Koi...or the 14K, otherwise bullets will have no eyes (no exact targets) and knives and bullets will have no feelings," said the unsigned letters, which were received by eight Chinese-language daily newspapers and a television station on Friday.
Lei Pang-chue, president of the Macau Chinese Press Workers Association, said the letters posed a "very serious threat" to press freedom in Macau.
But he stressed the enclave's media would "continue to write about all the things that the public needs to know".
Police said they were investigating the letters.
A senior police official said on Friday the district court had recently issued an arrest warrant for Wan, the alleged leader or "dragonhead" of the 14K.
The enclave returns to Chinese rule on December 20, 1999.
